why: Moves are data, played by the renderer over a plate’s published slots; see engine/motion.js for each move’s per-frame function. No move fades (rule 2).

moves.appliesTo: any figure or callout slot whose text is one number

moves.how: clip the data layer to reveal(plotArea, t, "left-linear"); the accent point appears on the last frame
clip each column to reveal(box, t_i, "bottom"), t_i staggered by one frame, the attention column last

moves.appliesTo: a slot with underline, or the quote slots
moves.how: the underline rect width = reveal(box, t, "left").w

moves.appliesTo: any one slot; the "this one" beat
moves.how: penCircle(box) stroked in attention with penDash(len, t)

moves.appliesTo: paper plates; the push in on a footnote
every room angle with a screen, glow or lamp
moves.how: screen and glow take their shade tone where SCREEN_PULSE[f]; lamp where LAMP_FLICKER[f]

moves.appliesTo: angles with a window pane; December, with the Christmas set
moves.how: snow(pane, f) as paper-role dots inside the pane, drawn behind the frame bars

moves.appliesTo: angles with a window pane; a gloomy episode
moves.how: RAIN(pane, f) as short glow-shade strokes inside the pane

moves.appliesTo: the board angles; a new card on the wall of calls
moves.how: the card translated pinDrop(t).dy and rotated pinDrop(t).rot about its pin
translateX(slideX(width, t)); out is the same move reversed
old number at tick(h, t).oldY, new at .newY, both clipped to the slot

anchors.why: Where each move lands on each plate, READ from its published slots by motion.anchorFor(); null = the plate has nothing for that move, skip it. Never placed by eye.
